issues: The corrected rationale and change log implicitly disclose the gold label by repeatedly asserting the comment deserves the top rubric level (score 5), e.g., 'matching the top level of the rubric' and 'an explicit, concretely specified action corresponds to the highest rubric category.' This reveals the final score/gold label.

While correcting the errors, the rationale overstates concreteness and effectively constructs its own argument rather than neutrally describing the actionability of the comment, inventing framing ('The comment also grounds the request by pointing out precisely why...') that goes beyond the source material.
The change log entries partially function as justifications that echo the gold label mapping (e.g., 'corresponds to the highest rubric category') instead of purely describing the edit.
parsed.review_summary: The candidate fixes the identified error targets by rejecting the prior score-3 conclusion and arguing for a higher score, but it does so by explicitly referencing the rubric levels and effectively leaking the gold label. It also adds interpretive content not grounded in the source material. A safe revision should avoid naming or implying any numeric rubric level and should not editorialize about the correct score.
